newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rise, outlook for next week unclear.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rise, outlook for next week unclear.

text.p: Polish shares on Friday rose in higher turnover after Thursday's fall but analysts said the slightly stronger selling after price fixing made it difficult to predict the market's performance next week.
"We could have growth on Monday...but I'm not inclined to believe we'll beat our July (27-month) high next week," said Cezary Markiewicz, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.
Analysts said Friday's higher turnover was a good sign but that it needed to be higher to signal the kind of heavy institutional buying that could sustain a significant growth trend.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.8 percent to 13,932 points and turnover rose 32.5 percent to 105.1 million zlotys ($38.3 million) on both markets. The July 5 high was at 14,282.2 points. Losers led gainers by 69 to two with six stocks flat.
Analysts said top gainer Petrobank, up 7.1 percent, may have been helped by Thursday's news that the industry ministry had cleared its sale of a majority stake to South Korea's LG Group.

They were surprised by the scale of mass privatisation NFI units' 9.8-percent rise. The units rose 6.7 percent in heavy 2.7-million-zloty ($1 million) continuous trade, where all five stocks either closed flat or did not trade.
